format: Internal preparation document, not an official API payload
title: SUNSET — Support once. Share forever.
short_description: Pool capped sponsorship to release a verified offline learning resource, or claim a refund. Transfer a stewardship NFT to hand over recovery-mirror maintenance without restricting public access or changing who receives the funds.
problem: Useful lessons and practical guides are often unpaid or paywalled, and their future availability can depend on one operator. Communities need a capped public-release agreement that compensates makers, permits refunds when conditions fail and lets someone else maintain recovery.
demonstration: Open the verified live Released campaign and inspect the pinned contract/code hash.
Show finalized 0.06 + 0.04 testNEAR funding, matching release and native 0.1-testNEAR creator payout with completed callback.
Recover the original and steward-selected mirror against the same commitments; download the standalone game.
Show real NFT handover, former-owner mirror rejection and new-owner mirror selection.
Open the actual downloaded file in a fresh browser with browser network offline before load; complete all five questions.
Inspect both finalized deadline-expiry refund paths and their native withdrawals; keep protocol failure/max-state scenarios explicitly unverified.
evidence_status: Reviewed byte-identical testnet deployment; finalized exact funding/release/native creator payout, stewardship handover, and both actual expiry-refund paths with native withdrawals. Actual hosted original/mirror recovery and downloaded game completed 5/5 in a cold browser with browser offline enabled before file load. Protocol failure/max-state cases and independent-user/educator evidence remain pending.
differentiation_limits: Public buyouts, offline education and transferable maintenance authority have prior art. The prototype integrates verifiable release/refund, independent reuse and standard maintenance-token transfer. Demand and educational impact are not validated.

official_rules.submission_limit: One submission per project; at most two independent, disclosed projects per person/email. Saved entries need human organizer-reviewed correction requests, never resubmission.

official_submission_requirements: Public repository by the deadline, remaining public through judging, with a license and reproducible README; check history for secrets.
Human-published public X demo post with attached video or screenshots, the statement that it was built at NEAR HACKATHON, @NEARProtocol and #NEARHackathon.

Human-confirmed project name, lead name, contact email, exact team-size option, defensible track IDs, public repository URL, public X demo-post URL, mainnet prize-payout account and project description.
Read the exact contact notice, obtain consent, and obtain explicit approval of the full final payload before an agent sends it.
Submit once through the official form or API during the development window; do not commit a payload containing personal data.

remaining_engineering_validation_goals.interpretation: Internal quality goals, not additional organizer eligibility requirements. Disclose unverified behavior accurately.
